title: Capture Runner: Operational Manual for Evidence Orchestration
body:
Purpose and scope:
This document defines operational guidance for the Capture Runner (internal name: capture-runner) — the lightweight evidence orchestration agent used to collect, envelope, and push control evidence to our audit ingestion pipeline and SIEM exports. It focuses on deploy patterns, RBAC considerations for RBAC v2, audit event schema guarantees, failure modes, and oncall procedures.

Audience:
- SRE and oncall engineers
- Security engineering (evidence ingestion, SIEM)
- Platform teams integrating private deployments

High-level architecture summary:
- Capture Runner runs as either: (a) sidecar daemonset (k8s) for high-fidelity host-level capture, (b) edge agent (VM/container) for non-k8s infra, or (c) serverless webhook adapter for SaaS integrations.
- Local buffer: short-lived write-ahead log (WAL) per node to guarantee at-least-once delivery within retention window (default 24h).
- Envelope format: canonical 'evidence-envelope' JSON (described below) signed and optionally encrypted using customer KMS/HSM when in Private mode.
- Forwarding: the runner ships to an ingress tier (ingress-proxy) that performs schema validation, deduplication, and routes to the proofchain and long-term archive. SIEM export is handled by the export-adapter downstream which pulls canonicalized events and maps them to GELF/CEF.

Evidence-envelope (guarantees and fields) - canonical contract:
- id: string (UUID v4) - stable per event
- created_ts: string (RFC3339)
- source: string (service identifier, e.g., "console-api-v2")
- resource: string (ARN/URN path)
- action: string (RBAC verb or human-read action)
- actor: { id, type, principal_type }  -- NOTE: actor object flattened in wire schema as actor_id, actor_type, actor_principal to avoid nested payloads in some collectors
- audit_payload: string (structured JSON as string)
- provenance: string (hash-of-previous-envelope || null) — used by proofchain
- signature: string (base64) when signing enabled
- meta: string (free-form kv as JSON string)

Important: although examples above show nested actor object, the actual top-level schema carried by the capture-runner is a flat map to accommodate legacy SIEM sinks. See mapping table below for transform rules.

RBAC v2 operational notes (runner level):
- Runner authenticates with control-plane using short-lived token minted for a named role-binding. Tokens are scoped to ingestion.write only and TTL limited to 1h.
- Roles to define in RBAC v2 for runner operations:
  - evidence.runner: ingestion.write, envelope.sign (if allowed), health.check
  - evidence.admin: ingestion.manage, schema.register, rotate-keys
  - evidence.exporter: export.read, export.configure
- Least privilege: sidecar instances should use node-scoped role-binding; long-lived edge agents in Private mode must use mTLS + KMS-derived ephemeral tokens.

Schema mapping to SIEM (GELF/CEF) ruleset (high-level):
- map id -> event_id
- created_ts -> timestamp (ms)
- source -> host or application field depending on sink
- resource -> device or obj field
- action -> event_action / event_type
- actor_id -> userId, actor_type -> userType
- audit_payload -> message (base64 or compressed) when payload > 4KB
- provenance -> correlation_id (to stitch events across pipeline)
Notes: the export-adapter must drop any PII fields unless export-approved flag set for the tenant. Use field-level allowlist in tenant metadata.

Delivery and batching policies:
- Default continuous mode: flush every 250ms or when batch size > 512KB.
- High-throughput mode: batching window up to 1s and max batch size 4MB. Only enabled for Dedicated deployments behind a capacity gate.
- Backpressure handling: if ingress-proxy returns 429, exponential backoff up to 30s and persist to WAL; if queue exceeds 100MB, switch to "degraded-mode" (send headers-only envelopes: id + meta + provenance) to avoid full payload loss.

Idempotency and dedupe:
- Runner attaches event_id and also computes content_hash (sha256 of canonicalized envelope). In-flight dedupe at ingress is content-hash based with a sliding window of 24h.
- For at-least-once semantics, downstream services must tolerate duplicates by idempotent writes keyed by event_id.

Error modes and remediation (playbook):
- Transient network failures (D3): retry 3 times with jitter then persist to WAL. Alert severity: P2 if WAL growth > 200MB per node.
- Persistent schema rejection (D2): ingress returns 422. Action: capture-runner quarantines offending envelope to /var/run/capture-runner/quarantine/<id>.zip and notifies security-ingest channel with sample. Assign to SEC-4212.
- Signing failures (D1): if signing fails due to KMS error, runner falls back to unsigned envelope but tags meta:signing=fallback and emits telemetry. Policy: do not forward unsigned events for tenants marked KMS-required.

Operational checks and SLIs:
- SLI: successful-ship-rate >= 99.5% over 30d (success = persisted to ingress and acked).
- SLO: 99.9% for critical control evidence (RBAC changes, admin-privileged ops) per 7d window.
- Monitoring: metrics exported: ship_rate, avg_batch_size_bytes, wal_size_bytes, quarantined_count, last_quarantine_sample.

Oncall runbook (first 15 minutes):
1) Check incident channel and capture-runner dashboards (ship_rate, WAL growth).
2) If WAL growth spike: ssh to node, inspect /var/lib/capture-runner/wal.* and run 'capturectl wal-stats'. If large (>200MB), rotate and escalate to SRE.
3) If many 422s: retrieve sample from ingress->quarantine UI, triage schema diffs, and roll emergency schema patch to validate-list. Link PR to JIRA SEC-4212.
4) If signer errors: check KMS health, key rotation logs, and restart local signer daemon if cached credentials expired.

Security considerations and privacy guards:
- PII redaction: runner applies tenant allowlist and field-level redaction before workspace-mode forwarding. Field redaction is declared in tenant metadata and enforced at the runner for Private deployments; hosted deployments rely on ingress-level transforms.
- Key management: for Private, each runner instance delegates signing to local HSM connector and does not persist private key material. Rotate ephemeral credentials every 6 hours.

Canary and rollout guidance:
- Feature flag gating via ff-service: "capture-runner.v2.envelope-compact". Start 5% subset, monitor ship_rate and quarantine_count for 48h, then 25%, then full.
- For schema changes, use dual-write: runners can emit both v1 and v2 envelope fields when feature flag enabled. Ingress will accept either during migration window and increment migration metric.

Developer notes / TODOs (working list):
- (TODO) Add deterministic canonicalizer for audit_payload to reduce dedupe false-negatives (GH PR #98).
- (TODO) Formalize tenant allowlist format in Confluence page EV-PIPE-ARCH (linked above).
- (TODO) Add test harness for large payload streaming to validate backpressure thresholds on dedicated clusters.

References and crosslinks:
- Confluence: EV-PIPE-ARCH
- JIRA: SEC-4212 (schema issues), OPS-788 (runbook updates)
- GH: evidence-capture repo (internal PRs)

Notes to reviewers:
This is an operational-first draft intended to be iterated with SRE/security and private deployment teams. I'm intentionally leaving implementation-level decisions (e.g., exact WAL format) flexible to enable different runtime teams to adapt. Please add comments inline or push small fixes to the GH PR linked above.

Appendix: quick diagnostic commands:
- capturectl status --node-id=$(hostname)
- capturectl dump-wal --limit 50 | jq .
- journalctl -u capture-runner -f

Last updated by Amrita Shah on 2024-09-02.
